What if you wore a tight ponytail every single day?
It's quick, neat and keeps hair off your face. Pulling your hair back hard puts constant tension on the roots. Some people even get headaches from a ponytail that's too tight.

But here's the twist. Over time, that pulling can cause traction alopecia, a type of hair loss along the hairline that can become permanent. Doctors suggest loosening it, changing its position often, and using soft scrunchies instead of tight bands. The good news is that if you catch it early, the hair usually grows back.
